ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: start here
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What Rimfolk adds to your colony, and where to find it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: You don't need all of it on the first day. Answer the wishes and see what the colonists do.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
Rimfolk turns your colonists into a small society. They ask for things and remember what you did about it, make friends and rivals, keep journals, dream, and wear down under hard times. A council helps you keep up: an advisor that points out what the colony needs, and meetings where the colony picks a goal to work toward.
All of it lives in the council window. Open it with the council button in the bottom bar; it opens on This week, the page of what needs you (the mod settings can make it come back to the page you were on instead).

points.li: Start each day on This week (the first page of the Colony section). It lists what waits on you (wishes and petitions, oldest first, letters that want an answer, promises at risk), what's coming (gatherings, days on the calendar, fights, missions, a camp) and how people are (strain, serious illness, trust, the balance of Rimfolk's moods). Click a line to go where it leads.
Look at Priorities (in the Colony section) now and then. It lists what the colony needs, worst first.
Answer wishes as they come. Grant one by making it happen, promise it to buy time, or refuse it. A refusal costs less than a wish left to lapse.
Select a colonist and open their Mood tab to see what weighs on them and what would help, or their Story tab for everything Rimfolk knows about them.
About once a quadrum the council meets in the evening. Keep people at home that day if their say matters to you.

The smaller news (new friends, quirks, birthdays, ailments, a story moving on) comes together in one Colony news letter each evening, with a button to go where each happened. Letters that ask you to decide, and serious news, still come at once; the Colony news setting can show it all as it happens instead, or send it only to the History tab.

li.heading: Finding your way around the council window

points.li: People, then Everyone: every colonist in one table, with mood and Rimfolk's share of it, trust and how it moved this week, strain, the setbacks weighing on them and what helps, their wish, their personal story, health and quirks. Click a heading to sort; hover a cell for more; click a row to select the colonist.
Council, then Dilemmas: the questions waiting for an answer, the traditions the answers founded, and every answer since with how it went.
Pin a colonist or a wish to keep it at the top of This week: the pin shows when you hover a line there, a row in Everyone, a wish card, or a colonist's page in the roster.
"Mark all read" on This week (or "Put all news away" in a news letter) clears the evenings' colony news from the letter stack; it stays in the History tab.
Each page remembers its filter and sort order. Options, then Keyboard, has optional shortcuts for the council's pages under "Rimfolk"; none is set until you pick a key.

li.heading: Too much at once?
li.text: Every part has its own switch in the mod settings (Options, then Mod options, then Rimfolk), on seven pages with a search box over them, and a line under each switch says what you'll notice with it on. Four presets set many at once: light touch, story-rich, demanding and default, each listing what it changes before it does. The Stakes setting decides how much it all matters: Gentle has only upsides, and Advisor only has no mood effects at all.

li.heading: Reading on
li.text:
The pages below explain the main parts. Each one ends with its own links, like this page.
If the text is too small or too cramped, the Aa buttons at the top of the almanac set its text size (Small, Normal, Large or Larger, also in the mod settings), and the « button beside them folds the lists away so a page gets the whole width. Tables too wide for the page show each row as a small card.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: checking that it works
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Where to look to see each of the newer features at work.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Most of these wait for their moment: a happy colonist, a long day of hauling, an evening meeting.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A short list for checking that Rimfolk's newer parts are running in your game. Each one says where to look and what you should see. Most need their setting on, and a few need the deeper game hooks.

points.li: Good times: open the Mood tab of a happy colonist (above 75% mood). Under the mood bar, a faint "Good times" line says what Rimfolk's balance takes off their good moods right now. Hover it for the rules.

Ailments: after a long day of hauling, mining or building, a colonist now and then gets a strained back, and after long bench work sore hands. It shows in their Health tab, and its description says what helps. The game's disease events also bring head colds and stomach bugs.

Visual touches: on a comet night the sky takes a faint cool cast, firefly nights bring small green-gold blinks around colonists outside after dark, and a council meeting opens with a bell. Only on the map you're looking at.

Meetings: on the Ambition page, call a council meeting. At the set time colonists put down their work and walk over, and sleepers are woken and come late. The letter at the end says who came, who was late and who missed it, and why.
The heart in RimHUD: in RimHUD's settings, Content tab, "Add third-party" lists Rimfolk's lines (strain, feelings, the heart's needs) and bars. Once added, they show in a colonist's RimHUD panel.

Personal stories: once one begins (a message names it), the colonist's Story tab has a "Personal story" section with the stage it has reached and what it waits for next. Each stage adds a journal line and a chronicle line; a talk the story waits on shows in the social log. In development mode, "Personal story: begin one for..." starts one for a colonist it fits, and "Personal story: next stage" moves it on.

The colony calendar: open History, then Calendar. Founding day is there from the start, and long-serving colonists' birthdays after two years. Name a day for today with "Name a day": within the hour (in the daytime) its letter comes, and keeping it starts a party, games or a rest day.

Material counts: open a room plan and look at its materials. Each shows green with some to spare and amber when it only just covers the room. In the game's build menu, a wall's material list reads like "Steel wall 420 (+85 lying around), enough for 84".

What colonists say: keep the camera on the colony for a few hours. Now and then someone says a short line over their head about how they are: a strong feeling (the Heart section of their Story tab says which), an ailment from their Health tab, a setback from their Mood tab, a calendar day tomorrow, a wish still open. The same colonist speaks about once a day at most. It shows as the setting "Colonists' speech shows as" says: speech bubbles with Interaction Bubbles, else floating text.

Gatherings: at a bonfire the fire smokes, and sparks after dark; at a toast, a while in, a small warm glint goes up over every head at once; at a grave after dark, while someone remembers there, a low warm glow shows by the stone. A calendar day's letter is followed by a small bell.

Small habits: after a death, watch the one who grieves in their free time; the job line in their inspect pane reads "visiting (name)'s grave". A convalescent's reads "taking a slow walk", and after a raid the ones who fought may be "sitting by the fire after the fight" if the colony has a lit campfire.

The weather: when the first snow of a winter falls (after ten days or more without any), a heat wave or cold snap begins, or a storm rolls in, someone in view says something about it, and a line may turn up in a journal. In the two days after the first snow, children may go out to build snowmen.

li.heading: When something doesn't show
li.text:
Check its setting first. Then turn on development mode (Options), open the debug actions and pick "Rimfolk: check myself" under Rimfolk. It lists which game hooks took, which parts are switched on and which of your mods Rimfolk found. A screenshot of it says a lot in a bug report.
Development mode also has shortcuts for testing: "Heart: add 20 strain" moves a colonist's strain bar, the comet and firefly nights can be started from the incident list, and "Calendar: a day comes round now" brings any day on the calendar round at once.
